text: With scope locked, this is the first real architecture decision: which Azure SQL option actually hosts PolicyClaimsDB going forward.

An Azure VM hands back the same OS-patching and hand-built-restore risk that caused the original incident. Managed Instance's extra surface area isn't a need this database has. Azure SQL Database matches the workload directly.
PolicyClaimsDB is one self-contained database with no cross-database dependencies, run by a small team with no appetite for a second server to patch and babysit by hand.

The naming is fixed from here forward: resource group rg-thornridge-sql-prod, primary server thornridge-sql-server, database PolicyClaimsDB -- with a secondary server and failover group arriving in a later lesson.
The platform is chosen. Next: planning the actual migration path with Data Factory.
